ALL LIVE. FTSE closed 16:35 BST at 10,458.50 -0.79 — the feed returned the live close correctly, unlike the
last three mornings, which confirms the lag is confined to the first half-hour after the London open.
Wall Street open, so .SPX and .VIX are live intraday values, not carried closes.

GILT — basis declared, because the feed is unusable here.
CNBC's previous_day_closing for UK10Y-GB read 5.4493 at 17:51, IDENTICAL to the live price, i.e. the field
had become self-referential. It cannot be used to compute a daily change. Trading Economics showed 5.45
with a change of +0.048, which implies a prior of 5.401 and does NOT reconcile with Tuesday's close.
Published change is computed against Tuesday's independently established close of 5.3775, the same basis
this morning's edition used:
  this morning  5.4333 - 5.3775 = +0.0558 -> +0.06 (published 5.43)
  this evening  5.4362 - 5.3775 = +0.0587 -> +0.06 (published 5.44)
Both round to +0.06, so the series is internally consistent across today's two editions.
Intraday high was 5.4493 at 17:51; it eased to 5.4362 by 18:05.

ADDENDUM after corroboration pass (NBC, 15:47 BST): the earlier ft.com-vs-CNBC conflict is resolved —
BOTH were right, on different snapshots. Session highs were 10-year 5.35% and 30-year 5.73%, the highest
for each since 2002; CNBC's 5.307/5.684 at 16:39 were later settled levels. The drivers carry the session
highs and the published ticker carries the 18:05 level (5.292). Also new: the UK 30-year gilt reached its
highest since 1998, which is the sharper domestic line and is now in the Gilt driver.
